column1: # bigram_priors.tsv -- the authored half of the `bigrams` table.
# The other half is counted from `lexicon.txt` by a deterministic script
# (`ocrcer-build`'s `bigrams` module), so that half needs no numbers typed
# here. What a word list cannot tell you is everything OUTSIDE a word: how
# digits run together, what a decimal point sits between, that `Ø` precedes a
# number and `°` follows one, that `M8x1.25` is an ordinary string in this
# domain. That is what this file supplies.
# EVERY WEIGHT BELOW IS AN AUTHORED GUESS and the whole file is on chunk 8's
# tuning list. They are pseudo-counts on the same scale as the counts taken
# from the lexicon, so a weight of 100 says "about as much evidence as a
# hundred occurrences in the word list". What is defensible is the ORDER: that
# a digit is followed by a digit far more often than by a letter, that a
# currency sign is followed by a digit and almost nothing else, that a word
# rarely starts with a math symbol. The exact magnitudes are not measured and
# are not presented as if they were.
#   default  <weight>                     every category pair not named below
# Categories are the charset's own `category` column plus `^`, the word
# boundary: `^` as a prev means the start of a word and as a next means the
# end of one. A literal character column holds one character; `^` there is
# the boundary and is written as the two characters `\b` to keep it distinct
# After a lowercase letter, overwhelmingly another lowercase letter or the end
# of the word. An uppercase letter mid-word is the rare camel-case case.
# After an uppercase letter both an acronym continuing and a word continuing
# After a digit. This row is the one that carries the CAD and invoice domain:
# a number continues, terminates, or takes a separator or a unit mark.
# A currency sign is followed by a number and by essentially nothing else.
# A decimal point and a thousands separator, which is where the digit/punct
# Dimension and part-number syntax. `x` between digits is `M8x1.25` and
# `100x50`; the word list cannot supply it because it is not a word.
# Unit and annotation marks that attach directly to a number.
# The identifier heads this domain writes constantly: a capital letter
